evidence: src/domain/order.ts: Order.advance() and Order.cancel() call nextStateOf/isCancellable from src/domain/order-state.ts, so transition rules live in one place (NEXT_STATE, CANCELLABLE)
src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: StockReservationService.reserve uses product.canReserve(quantity) and product.reserve(quantity) from src/domain/product.ts, so it never changes stock directly
src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: constructor injects ProductRepository (src/domain/product-repository.ts), the module's own persistence port
src/domain/order-item.ts: the positive-integer quantity rule appears only in the OrderItem constructor
src/domain/product.ts: the non-negative stock rule appears only in the Product constructor; canReserve is the single reservation check
src/domain/errors.ts: ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError and InvalidStateTransitionError all extend DomainError and are used consistently across the module
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The src/domain module covers one concern: orders and product stock. That includes the entities (Order, OrderItem, Product), the order lifecycle (order-state.ts), the domain errors (errors.ts), the persistence and ID ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, IdGenerator) and one domain service (StockReservationService) that coordinates stock across products.

Each rule lives in one place:
- The state transitions and the list of cancellable states live only in order-state.ts. Order.advance and Order.cancel call nextStateOf and isCancellable rather than redefining them.
- The rule that an item's quantity must be a positive integer lives only in the OrderItem constructor.
- The rule that stock must be a non-negative integer lives only in the Product constructor.
- The rule for whether a quantity can be reserved lives in Product.canReserve.

StockReservationService works only through the module's own abstractions. It uses the ProductRepository port and Product's methods (canReserve, reserve, release) and never changes stock directly. Its pre-check calls product.canReserve, so the reservation rule is not copied. The pre-check exists so the service can reserve every item or none. It throws InsufficientStockError with the same message text that Product.reserve uses. That repeats an error message, not a rule, so it is not a violation. All files throw errors from the shared DomainError family, so error handling is consistent.
